part.text:
[
  {
    "type": "ambiguity",
    "quote": "When the caller pins only the worker CLI, use that CLI's default route or a more specific fleet route on it. Mark the lane `Unrouted` when none fits.",
    "scenario": "Caller pins Grok for a difficult-refactoring lane; Grok's default route exists (Grok 4.7 at `high`), but its keep-for list is 'Independent challenge and live web or X research', its entry says 'Do not use it as a coding fallback', and no lane row lists a Grok route for implementation.",
    "policy_answer": "None clear: the pin rule says use Grok's default route or a more specific route 'on it', but the fleet entry disqualifies Grok for coding, and 'none fits' is never defined.",
    "fix": "Define 'none fits' (for example, a lane type outside the CLI's keep-for column means Unrouted) and state whether a pinned CLI may use lane-row fallbacks on other worker CLIs."
  },
  {
    "type": "gap",
    "quote": "OpenCode | Set by the lane table | Set by the lane table | Open-weight, multimodal, and low-cost lanes",
    "scenario": "Caller pins OpenCode for a difficult-implementation or architecture-planning lane; no lane row lists an OpenCode route for those lanes.",
    "policy_answer": "None: OpenCode's default route and escalation are both 'Set by the lane table', which is circular, so the pin rule can only mark the lane Unrouted even though fleet models like GLM-5.3 can implement.",
    "fix": "Give OpenCode a concrete default (for example GLM-5.3 at `max`), or state that pinned-OpenCode lanes are Unrouted outside the rows that list OpenCode routes."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Budget-sensitive bounded coding or repository sweeps | Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol at `medium` | Sonnet 5.5 at `medium` or `high`; GLM-5.3 Flash at `max`; Opus 5.5 at `low`",
    "scenario": "Caller states a cost limit for a bounded but non-trivial coding lane; GPT-6.1 Sol, Sonnet 5.5, and GLM-5.3 Flash are all unavailable, so the last fallback is Opus 5.5 at `low`.",
    "policy_answer": "The budget row routes the lane to Opus 5.5 at `low`, but both the skill ('Routes whose range starts at `low` permit it only for trivial, readily checked tasks') and the Opus entry ('Use `low` only for trivial, readily checked tasks') forbid `low` for non-trivial bounded coding.",
    "fix": "Change the row's Opus entry to `medium`, or scope the `low` entry to trivial, readily checked tasks only."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Use `max` when the caller requires one worker or a fixed delegation structure.",
    "scenario": "Caller pins Codex with GPT-6.1 Sol and requires exactly one worker (no sub-delegation) for a hard coding lane.",
    "policy_answer": "Contradictory: the skill mandates `max`, but the GPT-6.1 Sol entry says prefer `xhigh` over `max` for coding unless a local sample shows a gain, Fable says prefer `xhigh`, and Sonnet 5.5 (`low` to `high`) has no `max` in range at all.",
    "fix": "Reword to 'do not use delegation modes; choose the highest in-range effort the fleet entry recommends for that model'."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Cost-sensitive agentic coding, automation, multimodal review, or structured technical prose | OpenCode with GLM-5.3 Flash | GPT-6.1 Sol at `medium`; Sonnet 5.5 at `medium`; Muse Spark 1.3",
    "scenario": "Caller requests cost-sensitive agentic coding; GLM-5.3 Flash, GPT-6.1 Sol at `medium`, and Sonnet 5.5 at `medium` are unavailable, so the next fallback is Muse Spark 1.3.",
    "policy_answer": "The row routes terminal-heavy agentic coding to Muse Spark 1.3, while the Muse entry says 'It trails on terminal-heavy agent work.'",
    "fix": "Remove Muse Spark 1.3 from the agentic-coding part of this row, or restrict its use here to the multimodal-review and prose lane types."
  },
  {
    "type": "ambiguity",
    "quote": "GPT-6.1 Sol at `low` or `medium`; GLM-5.3 Flash",
    "scenario": "Caller requests narrow high-volume extraction or triage; GPT-6 Luna is unavailable, so the orchestrator reaches the 'GPT-6.1 Sol at `low` or `medium`' fallback and must pick one effort (the same pattern appears as 'Sonnet 5.5 at `medium` or `high`' in the budget row).",
    "policy_answer": "None: the row offers two efforts with no selection rule, and the cost/latency tie-breakers apply 'between routes', not between efforts of one route.",
    "fix": "Pin one effort per fallback step (for example `medium`), or state 'choose the cheapest effort that still meets the model floor'."
  },
  {
    "type": "gap",
    "quote": "Cyber safeguards send most security work to Opus 4.8, which is outside this fleet. Use Opus 5.5 only for defensive review of the caller's own code.",
    "scenario": "Caller requests defensive security review of their own code; Daybreak Blue, GPT-6 Astra, and GPT-6.1 Sol are unavailable, so the lane routes to Opus 5.5 and the safeguard redirects the run to Opus 4.8 (the same issue hits Sonnet fallbacks via 'Cyber safeguards send flagged security work to Sonnet 5').",
    "policy_answer": "None: no rule says whether to accept an out-of-fleet redirect, treat the route as unavailable and try the next fallback, or halt.",
    "fix": "Treat a safeguard redirect to an out-of-fleet model as an unavailable route and continue down the listed fallbacks."
  },
  {
    "type": "unsafe",
    "quote": "Prefer contributor routes after explicit acceptance of their data terms.",
    "scenario": "Caller requests multimodal analysis of proprietary screenshots through OpenCode/Muse; the Muse identifier order starts with `meta/muse-spark-1.3-contributor`, and no rule says who must accept the data terms (caller, user, or the orchestrator itself) or how acceptance is recorded.",
    "policy_answer": "Only 'Prefer contributor routes after explicit acceptance' and 'Skip contributor routes when their data terms are not accepted'; silent on who accepts and how acceptance is verified, so an autonomous orchestrator can accept the terms itself and route private data through a contributor route.",
    "fix": "Require caller- or user-recorded acceptance before any contributor identifier, and default to the non-contributor identifiers otherwise."
  },
  {
    "type": "contradiction",
    "quote": "Use lower-cost models from other families to find edge cases and confirm results. Treat their findings as leads.",
    "scenario": "Caller requests the 'Edge-case discovery and confirmation across model families' lane (OpenCode with GLM-5.3, Muse Spark 1.3, or Kimi K3) to confirm a result across families.",
    "policy_answer": "Contradictory: the lane is named discovery and confirmation, but the same policy says these models' findings are 'leads, not verdicts' that must be reproduced before a stronger route acts on them, so the lane cannot deliver confirmation.",
    "fix": "Rename the lane to edge-case discovery only, and route actual confirmation to a stronger route or a reproducible check."
  },
  {
    "type": "ambiguity",
    "quote": "Use `grok-4.7-build-fast` only when latency matters and the host lists it.",
    "scenario": "Caller requests a latency-sensitive second-opinion lane; the host lists `grok-4.7-build-fast`, but no lane row or route table contains it, 'Use only the fixed fleet' is stated, and no effort range, fallback position, or reviewer pairing is defined for it (likewise GLM-5.3 Prime and GLM-5.3 FlashX, which get no permission rule at all).",
    "policy_answer": "None clear: the fleet entry authorizes the identifier while the fixed-fleet rule and the route tables exclude it.",
    "fix": "Add the faster-tier identifiers to the fleet table with effort ranges and pairing rules, or declare them aliases of their listed base routes."
  }
]
